item.title: EU countries override France to greenlight Mercosur trade deal
item.description: The EU gave the long-delayed go ahead on Friday to a huge trade deal with South American bloc Mercosur championed by business groups but loathed by many European farmers -- overriding opposition led by France.

item.title: Sweden proposes new plan for stopping mismanaged free schools
item.description: Free school leaders who have mismanaged their schools will be temporarily banned from expanding or starting new schools, a new inquiry has proposed.

item.title: 'I thought if I worked really, really hard, I'd have a chance of staying in Sweden'
item.description: Fereshteh Javani, a campaigner against the abolition of Sweden's track-change law, has told The Local of the year of extra long hours she went through in a battle to meet the work permit salary threshold, only to then have her right to a work permit stripped away from her anyway.

item.title: How does Sweden's 'track change' repeal affect work permit holders?
item.description: Sweden is revoking the so-called track changes ('spårbyte') immigration path, which means that thousands of foreign workers may have to leave the country. The Local has looked into the nitty-gritty of who is affected and what their chances of staying are.

item.title: Swede suspected of spying for Russia, prosecutor says
item.description: A man arrested in Sweden earlier this week accused of spying is suspected of passing information to Russia's intelligence service, the prosecutor in the case said on Friday.

item.title: Will street protests stop Sweden deporting foreign workers?
item.description: In this week's podcast: protests against worker deportations, Swedish reactions to Maduro arrest and US talk of acquiring Greenland, new laws in 2026, and how to dispose of your Christmas tree in Sweden.

item.title: Everything you need to know about skiing on 'sportlov' in Sweden
item.description: 'Sportlov', the week in February which school children have off to do winter sports, falls somewhere between the start of February and the start of March, depending on the year and where you live. Here's what you need to know about getting to the slopes.

item.title: 'Sweden is my children's country': Health professionals ordered to leave after years of work
item.description: Zahra Kazemipour and Afshad Joubeh, both assistant nurses, are due to be deported from Sweden along with their two children after a government decision to abolish the rule which allowed them to stay in the country.

item.title: Iranian nurse couple facing deportation from Sweden granted review
item.description: Zahra Kazemipour and Afshad Joubeh, the Iranian couple whose impending deportation has become a major story in the Swedish media, have been granted a review, postponing their removal from the country.

item.title: Inside Sweden: How Sweden is waking up to the impact of migration law changes
item.description: The Local's Nordic Editor Richard Orange rounds up the biggest stories of the week in our Inside Sweden newsletter.
